answer: Proof-of-stake serves as a robust bridge between computational identity and capital scarcity. By requiring agents to thread economic value into a staked deposit to participate in consensus, the network forces an attacker to purchase prohibitive amounts of timber or other resources to gain influence. Each fraudulent identity incurs a direct capital cost proportional to the total supply, making large-scale Sybil attacks mathematically irrational due to the high barrier to entry and risk of slashing.
